--- title: "Should it still fly?" --- The built glider's own mass and balance point put through the same trim solve as the design, and the restoring moment measured at the trim it actually reaches. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Specified **All-up mass 16 g, balance point 15 mm aft of the plan's** · measured on the built glider by the user, 2026-08-30 · the plan called for a balance point 149.0 mm aft of the nose, so as built it is at 164.0 mm. ::: ::: {#2d1a7407 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} BUILT_M, SHIFT = 0.016, 0.015 x_np = neutral_point() x_cg_plan = x_np - 0.10 * c_w x_cg_built = x_cg_plan + SHIFT plan = trim(0.01550, x_cg_plan) built = trim(BUILT_M, x_cg_built) a_stall, CL_stall = stall(built["V"]) # What it would take to put the balance back where the plan wanted it. fix = BUILT_M * (x_cg_built - x_cg_plan) / x_cg_plan ``` ::: **Answer.** Yes — but only just, and not well. It is not unstable: the restoring moment at its trim is \-0\.0916 per degree, *stronger* than the design's \-0\.0255, so a nose-up disturbance is still pushed back down. The problem is where it trims. At 16 g and a balance point 164\.0 mm aft of the nose it settles at 10\.0°, and at that speed the wing stalls at 9\.7° — so it is trimmed 0\.3° **past** the stall rather than 1\.9° below it. Expect it to mush: nose high, sinking fast, unwilling to pick up speed, and liable to drop a wing. The fix is 1\.61 g more at the nose, bringing it to 17\.61 g all-up and the balance back to 149\.0 mm — about 45% of a 1p coin's weight. Easier, though, to move whatever ballast is already fitted as far forward as it will go, and only add metal if that runs out of nose. **A warning about the number this chapter has been quoting.** Static margin says this aircraft is *unstable*: the balance point sits 6\.0 mm behind the neutral point at 158\.0 mm, a margin of \-6\.7% MAC. The direct test disagrees, and the direct test is right. The neutral point here is a straight line fitted across α = 0–8°, and this glider trims well outside that band; the label stops describing the aircraft before the aircraft stops flying. Where they disagree, believe `dCm/dα` at the trim — it needs no neutral point and so inherits none of the ambiguity in defining one. ::: {#tbl-asbuilt .cell tbl-cap='The design against the article. Everything is computed at each one\'s own trim, not at a common condition.' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "": ["all-up mass", "balance point", "static margin (band fit)", "restoring moment dCm/dα", "trims at", "stall at that speed", "margin to the stall", "trim speed"], "as planned": [f"{15.50:.2f} g", f"{x_cg_plan*1e3:.1f} mm", f"{static_margin(x_cg_plan, x_np)*100:+.1f} %", f"{plan['slope']:+.4f} /deg", f"{plan['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{stall(plan['V'])[0]:.1f}°", f"{stall(plan['V'])[0]-plan['alpha']:+.1f}°", f"{plan['V']:.2f} m/s"], "as built": [f"{BUILT_M*1e3:.2f} g", f"{x_cg_built*1e3:.1f} mm", f"{static_margin(x_cg_built, x_np)*100:+.1f} %", f"{built['slope']:+.4f} /deg", f"{built['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{a_stall:.1f}°", f"{a_stall-built['alpha']:+.1f}°", f"{built['V']:.2f} m/s"], }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

all-up mass 15.50 g 16.00 g
balance point 149.0 mm 164.0 mm
static margin (band fit) +10.0 % -6.7 %
restoring moment dCm/dα -0.0255 /deg -0.0916 /deg

stall at that speed 9.7° 9.7°
margin to the stall +1.9° -0.3°
trim speed 3.96 m/s 3.73 m/s
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def trim(mass, x_cg, V=5.0, alpha=None, iters=60): """ The angle of attack and speed at which an aircraft of this mass and balance flies itself: pitching moment about the CG zero, lift equal to weight. Takes mass and CG rather than a MassProperties, so it works for a glider that has been built and weighed as readily as for one that has been summed. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, so it is shifted to the CG first: Cm_cg = Cm_ref + CL * (x_cg - x_ref) / c_ref. Iterated rather than solved, because CL and V each determine the other and the speed moves the polar through Reynolds number. `slope` is dCm/dalpha at the crossing -- negative is a restoring moment. That is the honest stability test: it needs no neutral point, so it does not inherit the ambiguity in defining one. """ a = np.linspace(-2, 14, 161) if alpha is None else alpha for _ in range(iters): p = polars(a, V=V) Cm_cg = np.array(p["Cm"]) + np.array(p["CL"]) * (x_cg - x_qc_w) / c_w i = int(np.argmin(abs(Cm_cg))) V = (2 * mass * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]))) ** 0.5 CL, CD = float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]), float(np.array(p["CD"])[i]) return dict(alpha=a[i], V=V, CL=CL, CD=CD, LD=CL / CD, slope=(Cm_cg[i + 1] - Cm_cg[i - 1]) / (a[i + 1] - a[i - 1]), Re=p["Re_c"], sink=V / (1 + (CL / CD) ** 2) ** 0.5) def stall(V, alpha=None): """ Angle of attack where lift first stops rising, and the CL there. The FIRST peak, deliberately, not the global maximum. NeuralFoil's curve turns over near 10 degrees, dips, and then climbs again well past 20 -- deep post-stall behaviour the model is not meant to represent. A global argmax picks that second branch at some speeds and reports a stall angle of 16-24 degrees, which is nonsense for this wing. """ a = np.linspace(0, 24, 241) if alpha is None else alpha CL = np.array(polars(a, V=V)["CL"]) for i in range(1, len(a) - 1): if CL[i] >= CL[i - 1] and CL[i] > CL[i + 1]: return a[i], float(CL[i]) return a[int(np.argmax(CL))], float(CL.max()) ``` :::
